exposure: Caesarean section (CS) conducted before labour (prelabour CS (PLCS))
cohort: 255,227 women aged 15-49 years with singleton term births from 26 low-income and middle-income countries
finding: Compared to vaginal delivery, prelabor cesarean section was associated with increased neonatal mortality, decreased early breastfeeding and skin-to-skin contact, and longer hospital stay, but not significantly associated with early neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: The study found that planned cesarean section before labor (PLCS), compared with vaginal delivery, was associated with increased neonatal mortality, decreased early breastfeeding and skin-to-skin contact, and longer hospital stay in singleton term pregnancies in low-income and middle-income countries.
country: 26 low-income and middle-income countries (13 in Africa, 11 in Asia, and 2 in the Americas)
